results.title: Ballad to Cornwallis
results.creator_credit: Diane Beaudry, Ian McLaren, Rex Tasker and National Film Board of Canada
results.brief_description: Balladeer James Bennet satirises the history of Halifax in a song which he composed and sings in honour of the city’s founder. Clad in period costumes, Bennet travels through time against a background of old photographs and paintings, archival and contemporary film footage, until he ultimately finds himself in the midst of the city’s present-day building boom.

results.title: Balinese surfer 2: wave of change [Widescreen]
results.creator_credit: Bill Leimbach, Richard Flax, ABC-TV (Australia) and Lucky Country Productions
results.brief_description: In 1978, producer/director Bill Leimbach visited the Indonesian island of Bali and filmed a group of young Balinese boys who had discovered the art of surfing. This is the sequel to that film “Balinese surfer” as Bill and his production team revisit the original group, now all aged in their 40s, 25 years later. We follow their individual stories, the direction life has taken them, and how most of them still take time out to surf. Through personal narratives, intercut with footage from the original film, these Balinese men all express their concern for the environment, particularly with the enormous increase in tourism during the 80s and 90s. Their priority issues are with maintaining the supply of fresh water, and preventing sewage run-off into the ocean, reef bombing, and toxic gases from burning plastic. Bali is renowned for having some of the best waves in the world and through a program of surfing contests (attracting the international media), surfing magazines and an organization called Wave of Change, the focus is now on the next generation, who also surf, to be environmental ambassadors and promote the message for preservation of the marine environment and a policy of sustainable development in Bali and throughout the Indonesian islands. Narration - John Sheerin; Director of Photography - Simon Manzie.

results.title: Bag of rice = Kiseye berenj
results.creator_credit: Mohammad-Ali Talebi, Mari Iwata, Uta Miyamoto and Digital Media Lab, Inc
results.brief_description: Nobody seems to have time for four year old Jairan. She is from a large Tehranean family, where her parents have to work and her brothers and sisters are all too busy with their homework. One day she manages to convince her neighbour, Mrs Khanoom, to take her on a shopping expedition for a bag of rice. This proves to be demanding feat when, after making their way through the busy streets of Tehran, they find that the shop has already closed.

results.title: Bad by design: designers break the rules
results.creator_credit: Damien Ledwich, Jo Forsyth, Terry Murphy, Australian Film Commission, Blurred and Film Queensland
results.brief_description: From the Australian Film Commission’s Micro Docs Series II, Bad by Design explores the designing and creative process of three Australian designers; Max Bannah (Animator), Elisabeth Watson-Brown (Architect) and Mimmo Cozzolino (Graphic Designer). They reveal their goals with their work and how they’ve made their unique vision and approach succeed. All are highly accomplished in their own right and give the viewer a glimpse of their motivations and creative outlook. Illustrative animations by Damien Ledwich based on the Designers are intermixed throughtout.

results.title: Bad boys of Hollywood
results.creator_credit: Scott Marvel, Matthew Hane and Amvest Video
results.brief_description: ‘Bad boys of Hollywood’ provides an irreverent look at the changing face of Hollywood and the men who contributed to the ‘bad boy’ image of Hollywood during the 20th Century. Errol Flynn is featured with behind the scenes stories of his drinking, philandering and devil may care mischief making. Sean Penn gives meaning to the phrase “Let’s party!” and Steve McQueen provides a bunch of Hollywood producers with his version of ‘piss-take’ humour. Presented are many stories about these bad but lovable rogues, men who symbolised a changing society and reached iconic status for their off-screen antics. Narrated by Jeff Lupetin this video also features: Ronald Reagan, Marlon Brando, Robert Mitchum, Jack Nicholson, James Dean and John Belushi. WARNING: POOR QUALITY SOUND LEVEL

results.title: Balablok
results.creator_credit: Brent Walker Film Productions, Rene Jodoin and National Film Board of Canada
results.brief_description: An animated replay of the human comedy as amusing in its perception as in the way it caricatures man’s propensity to resort to violence rather than reason. The whole area of conflict is reduced to its simplest dimensions - cubes and balls representing opposing protagonists. Why they fight and what happens after the battle is a parody of human nature. A film without commentary. (Awards: Palme d’Or, Cannes; Colombo; Buenos Aires)

results.title: BadJelly the witch
results.creator_credit: Anne Wood, Norma Farnes, Norma Farnes Management and Ragdoll Productions
results.brief_description: Spike Milligan narrates this animated story of two children in search of a lost cow and the adventures this leads them to. They come across interesting and friendly animals who indeed save them from the nasty witch, BadJelly, and her hungry, nasty friend. All ends up well for the children and their cow. Spike Milligan wrote the imaginative story as well as narrates.

results.title: Bad girls. Series two. Discs 1 & 2 [DVD]
results.brief_description:
Episode number 1 of Series “Bad girls. Series two”.
Tug of love (wri. Maureen Chadwick, dir. Mike Adams): Helen is suspected of going AWOL and Jim’s eyeing off her job. Zandra goes into labour and complications ensue from her drug habit. Karen Betts (Claire King) returns to the wing. “Shit happens” (wri. Martin Allen, dir. Mike Adams): Jim’s wife is getting prank calls from Shell and Jim blames Nikki. Helen hands in her resignation and Fenner is temporarily stood down pending an investigation into an assault on Shell. “Visiting time” (wri. Mark Wadlow, dir. Laurence Moody): Karen Betts becomes Wing Governor. Yvonne helps Julie see her kids. Investigations are underway into the assault case against Shell. “Looking for love” (wri. Jayne Hollinson, dir. Laurence Moody): Dominic becomes Shell’s personal officer. Denny leaves the wing to visit her mother in hospital. The Julies help organise a romantic dinner. “Mistaken identity” (wri. Maureen Chadwick, dir. Laurence Moody): Group therapy sessions begin and HIV+ Mad Tessa Spall arrives on the wing. Fenner and Atkins form a mutually beneficial alliance. Wade gets a new roommate. “Losing it” (wri. Martin Allen, dir. Jim O’Hanlon): Sylvia’s given a new exercise regime and Zandra finally gets glasses. Barbara is feeling uncomfortable living with Nikki. Josh and Crystal’s relationship is progressing and Shell starts an anti-male campaign. Helen’s back on the ward working with area management, meaning she can spend more time with Nikki. “The Set up” (wri. Phil Ford, dir. Jim O’Hanlon): Shell’s under observation in the medical ward. Zandra collapses and further investigation is required to find out what’s wrong. Fenner’s being blackmailed by Atkins but he has the last word. “Babes behind bars” (wri. Maureen Chadwick, dir. Jim O’Hanlon): Shell’s worrying about the safety of her children. It’s Crystal’s last week and Yvonne comes up with a way to earn a few extra quid. Barbara helps out by setting up the website, “Babes behind bars”. The results are back from Zandra’s test.
